name: Nathan Williams
bio: A Representative from New York; was born in Williamstown, Mass., December 19, 1773; attended the common schools in Bennington, Vt.; moved with his parents to Troy, N.Y., in 1786; studied law; was admitted to the bar in 1795; commenced practice in Utica, N.Y.; assisted in the establishment of Utica ,N.Y., Public Library; librarian for a number of years; president of the village corporation; president of the Manhattan Bank, N.Y.; district attorney for the sixth district, 1801-1813; elected as a Democratic Republican to the Ninth Congress (March 4, 1805-March 3, 1807); served in the War of 1812; member of the New York state assembly, 1816-1818 and in 1819; regent of the University of the State of New York from January 28, 1817-February 13, 1824; district attorney of Oneida County 1818-1821; delegate to the New York state constitutional convention, 1821; judge of the circuit court, 1823-1833; appointed clerk of the New York state supreme court, 1834; moved to Geneva, Ontario County, N.Y., where he died; died on September 25, 1835, ; in Geneva, Ontario County, N.Y.; interment in the ``Burying Ground,'' Utica, Oneida County, N.Y.; reinterment in Forest Hill Cemetery, Utica, N.Y.
